chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Bakr and Muhammad ibn Abi al-Subhan from Hafs from Umar ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa from Harun ibn Kharijah who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Count Sha'ban as twenty-nine days; if the sky is cloudy, then begin fasting in the morning; and if it is clear, and you look carefully and see nothing (the new moon), then begin breaking the fast in the morning."

If the intention behind it were not what we mentioned, namely resolving to fast it on the assumption that it is from Sha'ban, then one would be obliged to intend that it is from the month of Ramadan and not pay attention to whether the sky is cloudy or clear.

key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, month of fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.صَائِماً: Fasting (abstaining from food, drink, etc. from dawn to sunset)
key_terms.مُتَغَيِّمَةً: Cloudy (referring to the sky obstructing the view of the moon)
key_terms.مُصْحِيَةً: Clear/Clear sky (referring to the sky allowing the view of the moon)
key_terms.مُفْطِراً: Breaking the fast (ending the state of fasting)

ai.seo_question: How to determine if the 30th of Sha'ban is Ramadan or just Sha'ban when the sky is cloudy?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the ruling for the 'Day of Doubt' (Yawm al-Shakk), instructing believers to fast with the intention of Sha'ban if the sky is cloudy on the thirtieth, thereby avoiding the premature obligation of Ramadan. If the sky is clear and the moon is not sighted, one breaks the fast, confirming the month of Sha'ban. This precautionary measure ensures that the strict obligation of Ramadan is not assumed without definitive evidence, reflecting the Shia principle of distinguishing between voluntary and obligatory fasting in ambiguous circumstances.
